study type: Cross-sectional survey and retrospective review of registry data
exposure: labor induction methods (dinoprostone, misoprostol, cervical balloon)
induction of labor without a medical indication
outcome: cesarean section rate in women with induced labor
cohort: The study surveyed all delivery units in Norway and analyzed data from the Medical Birth Registry of Norway for women with induced labor.
finding: Despite significant changes in the preferred methods for induction of labor over a decade (to misoprostol and cervical balloon), the cesarean section rates in women with induced labors remained stable.
mod_finding: The changed induction methods for labor did not influence the cesarean section rates among women with induced labors.
